Findings triage (first grade): **HOLD as `finding`.**

- **Premise verified on `origin/main` @ `b954120`**: the array branch and its whole-set collapse are live — `predicate.ts:331` (`startsWith('[')`) → `:337` (`return []` in the catch). The filer's measurement (membership false for every row, zero warnings) stands.
- **Why hold, not promote**: dormant by producer — every `in` predicate in the four shipped metadata-admin forms uses literal string arrays, and the file header declares the literal-only subset, so no user hits this today. The filed dedup is solid (distinct from ui#4049's tail-return and objectstack#6936's `resolveValue` path).
- **Restart/promotion conditions**: (a) the objectstack#7659 publish-time refusal card just queued this hour covers the producer-side half of this family — if its shape extends to `in`-set elements, this card's diagnose-only half may be worth promoting alongside; (b) any authored form shipping a non-literal set element makes this live and it should promote immediately; (c) ROADMAP M9 (real CEL evaluator) dissolves it — check before promoting.
- **Not escalated to a decision**: the fail-open-vs-diagnose fork only needs ruling if promoted; the box is at capacity and this is dormant.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

## Zone 1 — triage's scope ruling

> Scope: diagnose in the array branch's `catch` (warn naming the unparseable element; whether to fail the whole predicate loudly vs per-element is the implementer's measurement against #4049's precedent). ⛔ **Not a widening of the declared subset** — paths inside brackets stay unsupported, they just stop failing silently. S / sonnet.

Read that last sentence twice. **A path inside brackets must still not work.** The card is about the *silence*, not the *capability*. If your change makes a non-literal element start resolving, you have implemented a different card — one that widens the accept set and would be `Clause-②: yes` with a maintainer decision behind it.

## The defect

`predicate.ts` — the array branch (`startsWith('[')`) has a `catch` that does `return []`. An `in` predicate whose set contains a non-literal element therefore collapses to the **empty set**, so membership is **false for every row**, with **zero warnings**. Silent wrong verdicts, which is the family #4049 just closed at `parseLiteral`'s tail — and the array branch provably never reaches that diagnostic.

Verified by triage on `origin/main` @ `b954120`; **re-verify on current main** — that was a week ago and this directory took two merges today.

## The one judgement triage left you

**Fail the whole predicate loudly, or diagnose per element?** Measure it against **#4049's precedent** rather than choosing on taste — that card set this family's posture and consistency with it is worth more than either option's local merits. Say in the report what #4049 does and why you matched or diverged.

## Dormancy is context, not a reason to be quiet

Triage graded this **dormant by producer**: every `in` predicate in the four shipped metadata-admin forms uses literal string arrays, and the file header declares the literal-only subset. So no user hits it today.

That is exactly why it is worth fixing **now and cheaply**: the diagnostic is the thing that will be there on the day someone authors a non-literal element. ⛔ Do not let dormancy tempt you into a bigger fix "while we're here" — no evaluator work, no widening, no refactor of the literal path.

Triage also recorded that **ROADMAP M9 (a real CEL evaluator) dissolves this card entirely.** If you discover M9 has landed or is landing, stop and report rather than building a diagnostic for a branch that is about to be replaced.

## Tests

- An `in` predicate with a **non-literal** element produces the diagnostic (assert on the message naming the element — a bare "it warned" pin will pass for any warning).
- An `in` predicate with **literal** elements is completely unaffected: same verdict, no warning. This is the pin that proves you did not widen or perturb the supported path.
- Whatever you chose on the loud-vs-per-element fork, pin the resulting verdict shape explicitly.
- Reverse-verify: restore the `catch`, keep the tests, predict the reds **before** running, report predicted vs observed.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only** — here derive from `.github/workflows` and `package.json`. If you add user-facing warning text, the i18n gates (`check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`) come into play — check whether this diagnostic is a `console.warn` (dev-facing, no i18n) or user-visible copy, and treat it accordingly. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`); `patch`, ⛔ never `major`.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn.**

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #4266`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.
